title: 🥒️ Norm step vocabulary
description: 🥒️ The ONE domain-neutral step grammar every norm `🥒️.feature` is written in. A template is literal text with `{name}` holes; both step layers (`🐍️.py`, `🦀️.rs`) match it by finding the literal segments in order, so no regular-expression dialect is shared. A family fixes the step sequence, the fields its holes bind and the shape of the projection both implementations emit and the comparison profile judges.

catalogue-fixture-case.law: A committed catalogue case is evaluated by both implementations; every value the oracle names is compared by the feature's profile.

steps.template: the committed catalogue case {fixture} at index {index}
both implementations evaluate catalogue entry {entry} on that case
every result named by the oracle agrees within the comparison profile

catalogue-example.law: A hand-checked catalogue example is reproduced by each implementation within its stated relative tolerance.

steps.template: the catalogue entry "{entry}" for annex "{annex}" with inputs "{inputs}"
the entry is evaluated
the output "{key}" equals {expected} within relative tolerance {tolerance}

clause-vector.law: A clause quantity of a committed vector equals the independent oracle value within the stated relative tolerance.

steps.template: the clause vector "{vector}" of "{part}"
the quantity "{quantity}" is evaluated
it equals the independent oracle value within relative tolerance {tolerance}

published-example.law: A quantity of a hand-checked worked example equals its published value within the stated relative tolerance.

steps.template: the worked example "{example}" with its published inputs
the quantity "{quantity}" is evaluated
it equals {expected} within relative tolerance {tolerance}

oracle-check.law: The utilisation a check reports on a committed showcase subject equals the independent oracle quantity.

steps.template: the showcase subject "{subject}" with the {annex} annex
the compliance report is evaluated
the utilisation of the check "{check}" equals the oracle quantity "{quantity}" within relative tolerance {tolerance}

check-outcome.law: A committed document fixture yields, for one check id, the committed status and utilisation.

steps.template: the committed document {fixture}
the check "{check}" is evaluated
its status is "{status}" with utilisation {utilisation} within relative tolerance {tolerance}

scene-law.law: A committed document fixture projects to a scene whose entities, handles and diagrams follow the stated laws.

steps.template: the committed document {fixture}
the scene is projected
entity "{entity}" is of kind "{kind}" with {handles} handles and {diagrams} diagrams

mutation-round-trip.law: A committed mutation applied to its before-snapshot and then inverted by its own computed inverse restores the before-snapshot exactly.

steps.template: the committed before-snapshot {before}
the committed mutation payload {mutation}
the mutation is applied and then its computed inverse
the document equals the before-snapshot

oracle-comparison.law: The Python oracle run on a committed input agrees with the kernel for every named quantity.

steps.template: the committed oracle input {fixture}
the Python oracle and the kernel both evaluate it
every quantity named by the oracle agrees within the comparison profile
